definition_zh: 充满活力的；鲜艳的；振动的
definition_en: full of energy and life; bright and strong in colour; or moving quickly to and fro
core_image: 拉紧的琴弦被拨动，来回震颤，发出明亮的声响与光彩
scene: 老街的市集上人声鼎沸，摊前的果子红得发亮。The market in the old street was vibrant, with loud voices and bright red fruit.
sceneCN: 这里 vibrant 是「充满活力的」（第 1 个义项：精力旺盛、生机勃勃）；句意：老街的市集充满活力，人声喧闹，果子鲜亮。

pos.zh: 充满活力的；生机勃勃的

derivatives.zh: 由名词性词干加动词后缀构成，义为「振动；颤动」
由 vibrate 加名词后缀构成，义为「振动」
由 vibrant 加名词后缀构成，义为「活力；鲜明度」
由 vibrant 加副词后缀构成，义为「充满活力地」

senses.title: Full of energy and life
senses.titleCN: 充满活力的；生机勃勃的
senses.definition: lively, energetic and full of activity, especially about a place, person or period
senses.definitionCN: 生动活跃、精力充沛、充满动态的，尤指地方、人或时期
senses.example: The old port has become a vibrant district of cafes and galleries.
senses.exampleCN: 这个老港区已变成布满咖啡馆与画廊的活力街区。
senses.why: The Latin verb vibrare means to shake or quiver, and a place that quivers with activity looks alive, so the shaking sense became liveliness.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词 vibrare 意为「抖动、颤动」，一个随活动而颤动的场所就像活了起来，于是「颤动」自然引申为「活力」。

senses.title: Bright and strong in colour
senses.definition: bright, strong and clear in appearance, as of a colour
senses.definitionCN: 外观明亮、浓烈而清晰，如颜色
senses.example: The walls were painted in vibrant shades of orange.
senses.exampleCN: 墙壁被刷成鲜艳的橙色。
senses.why: Vibration is the perceived property that makes light seem intense, so a colour that seems to vibrate reads as vivid and bright.
senses.whyCN: 在光学里，振动的强弱决定了光看起来有多强烈，因此仿佛在「振动」的颜色就显得鲜亮刺眼。

senses.title: Quivering or vibrating
senses.definition: rapidly moving to and fro, or full of quivering movement
senses.definitionCN: 快速来回移动的，或充满颤动感的
senses.example: A vibrant note rang out from the plucked string.
senses.exampleCN: 被拨动的琴弦发出一声震颤的音。
senses.why: This keeps the oldest physical core of the word, a rapid back and forth movement that can be felt or heard.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词最古老的物理本义：一种能被感觉到或听到的快速往复运动。

senses.title: Strong and resonant in sound
senses.definition: strong, resonant and carrying clearly, especially of a voice or sound
senses.definitionCN: 声音强劲、有共鸣、传得远，尤指嗓音或声响
senses.example: Her vibrant voice filled the whole hall.
senses.exampleCN: 她洪亮的嗓音充满整个大厅。
senses.why: Sound is a vibration in the air, so a voice that carries well is described as vibrant, more resonant than merely loud.
senses.whyCN: 声音本身就是空气的振动，所以传得远的嗓音被称作 vibrant，强调共鸣感，而不只是响亮。

senses.title: Full of vigorous ideas
senses.titleCN: 思想活跃的；富有创造力的
senses.definition: marked by vigorous thought, debate or creative activity
senses.definitionCN: 以有力的思想、辩论或创造性活动为特点的
senses.example: The city has a vibrant literary scene.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市有着活跃的文学氛围。
senses.why: Liveliness moves from streets to minds, so a scene of lively thought is still described with the same shaking energy.
senses.whyCN: 活力从街市转移到头脑里，思想活跃的场景仍然用同一种「震动」的能量来描述。

intro.en: Vibrant comes from Latin vibrare, to shake or quiver, through the present participle vibrans.
intro.cn: vibrant 来自拉丁语 vibrare（抖动、颤动），经由其现在分词 vibrans 进入英语。

items.en: Vibrare means to shake, quiver or brandish.
items.cn: vibrare 意为抖动、颤动或挥舞。

items.en: The participle vibrans means shaking or quivering.
items.cn: 分词 vibrans 意为抖动着的、颤动着的。

items.en: The adjective forme vibrante passes through French into English.
items.cn: 形容词形式 vibrante 经由法语进入英语。

items.en: Vibrant first describes things that quiver or move rapidly.
items.cn: vibrant 最初描述颤动或快速运动的事物。

items.en: Writers extend it to colours and sounds that seem to pulse with life.
items.cn: 作家们把它扩展到仿佛随生命脉动的颜色与声音。

items.en: Modern English makes vibrant a general praise word for lively places and people.
items.cn: 现代英语中 vibrant 成为称赞场所与人富有活力的通用词。

note.en: Vibrant is the shaking word that grew from strings to cities, close to vibrate and vibrancy, and to everyday words for lively and bright.
note.cn: vibrant 是「颤动」之词，从琴弦一路长到城市，与 vibrate、vibrancy 以及表示「活跃、明亮」的常用词相邻。

entries.definition: to move quickly to and fro
a continuous rapid movement to and fro
the quality of being full of life or bright colour
a slight rapid shaking of a singing or playing note
very bright and strong in colour or clear in the mind
not bright in colour and not interesting

normalIntro.en: Keep the physical picture of Latin vibrare, a string that shakes, and most senses of vibrant fall into place.
normalIntro.cn: 记住拉丁语 vibrare 那个「琴弦抖动」的物理画面，vibrant 的多数义项就都顺理成章了。

normal.en: Vibrant keeps Latin vibrans, the participle of vibrare, to shake.
normal.cn: vibrant 保留拉丁语分词 vibrans 的形式，源自 vibrare（抖动）。

normal.en: The verb vibrate and the nouns vibration and vibrancy share the same stem.
normal.cn: 动词 vibrate 与名词 vibration、vibrancy 共享同一个词干。

normal.en: A vibrant city is one that seems to shake with activity, vivid, energetic and busy.
normal.cn: vibrant city 指仿佛因活动而颤动的城市：鲜明、有劲、热闹。

normal.en: Vibrant colours are bright colours that seem to pulse, while a dull colour sits still.
normal.cn: vibrant colours 是仿佛在脉动的鲜亮颜色，而 dull 的颜色则沉静无光。

normal.en: Compare lively: lively is everyday, while vibrant often carries praise for places and colours.
normal.cn: 对比 lively：lively 更口语，vibrant 多用于赞美场所与色彩。

abstract.en: Picture a plucked string still quivering in the air as its note rings out.
abstract.cn: 想象一根被拨动的琴弦仍在空气里颤动，余音袅袅。

abstract.en: See a market awash with red fruit, yellow lanterns and dozens of voices.
abstract.cn: 想象一个市集，红果子、黄灯笼与满场人声扑面而来。

abstract.en: Imagine touching a guitar body and feeling the buzz run into your hand.
abstract.cn: 想象把手掌贴在吉他面板上，震动顺着指尖传进掌心。

examples.en: She loves living in a vibrant part of town with busy shops and street music.
examples.cn: 她喜欢住在城里热闹有趣的地段，那里店铺繁忙、还有街头音乐。

examples.en: The garden was full of vibrant flowers after the rain.
examples.cn: 雨后花园里开满了鲜艳的花朵。

examples.en: The whole room seemed to pulse with vibrant energy during the festival.
examples.cn: 节日期间，整个房间仿佛都涌动着蓬勃的活力。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「外」一下——琴弦「外」震得发亮，既振动又有活力；这只是拆音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 vibrare（抖动、颤动）+ 现在分词词尾 -ant → 法语 vibrante → 英语 vibrant，核心义「像琴弦一样颤动」，再引申出「有活力」与「色彩鲜明」。

sensesIntro.en: Vibrant starts as quivering movement, then lends its shaking energy to sound, colour and places, and finally to lively minds and scenes.
sensesIntro.cn: vibrant 从「颤动」这一运动本义出发，把抖动的能量依次借给声音、颜色与场所，最后延伸到活跃的思想与氛围。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a taut string still quivering after it is plucked.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根被拨动后仍在颤动的紧绷琴弦。

branches.en: Shaking energy becomes the liveliness of places and people.
branches.cn: 颤动的能量变成场所与人的活力。

branches.en: Colour that seems to vibrate reads as bright and vivid.
branches.cn: 仿佛在振动的颜色读起来就是鲜亮明艳。

branches.en: The literal quivering sense keeps the oldest physical core.
branches.cn: 字面的颤动义保留最古老的物理内核。

branches.en: A lively street and a lively mind both quiver with activity.
branches.cn: 热闹的街道与活跃的思想都因活动而「颤动」。

branches.en: Sound is a vibration in the air, so resonant voices are also vibrant.
branches.cn: 声音是空气的振动，所以有共鸣的嗓音也被称作 vibrant。

intro.en: Vibrant is built on the Latin stem vibr-, with English vibrate, vibration, vibrancy and the music term vibrato around it.
intro.cn: vibrant 建立在拉丁词干 vibr- 之上，周围有英语的 vibrate、vibration、vibrancy 以及音乐术语 vibrato。

latinIntro.en: Latin vibrare means to shake or quiver, and its participle vibrans gives the adjective its ending.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vibrare 意为抖动、颤动，其分词 vibrans 则为这个形容词提供了词尾。

items.example: Vibrare gives the shaking core of the word.
items.exampleCN: vibrare 提供这个词「抖动」的核心。

items.example: The participle ending -ant turns a verb into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 分词词尾 -ant 把动词变成形容词。

items.meaningCN: 有活力的；鲜艳的；振动的
items.example: Vibrant is the modern adjective of the family.
items.exampleCN: vibrant 是这个词族中的现代形容词。

items.meaning: to move quickly to and fro
items.example: Vibrate keeps the concrete action.
items.exampleCN: vibrate 保留具体的动作义。

items.meaningCN: 行为或状态的名词词尾
items.example: The suffix -ation forms vibration.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ation 构成 vibration。

items.example: Vibration names the movement itself.
items.exampleCN: vibration 指运动本身。

items.example: The suffix -cy forms vibrancy.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -cy 构成 vibrancy。

items.example: Vibrancy names the quality of being vibrant.
items.exampleCN: vibrancy 表示「有活力」这一性质。

items.meaningCN: 音乐术语中的意大利语词尾
items.example: The music term vibrato carries the same stem.
items.exampleCN: 音乐术语 vibrato 沿用同一词干。

items.meaning: a rapid slight shaking of a note
items.example: Vibrato applies the shaking to music.
items.exampleCN: vibrato 把颤动用于音乐。

definition_en: the area around a particular place or person, or the state of being near
core_image: 以一处房子为圆心，向外画一圈不大的范围，圈内都是「近邻」
scene: 学校周围几公里的村子都能听见回声。Several villages in the vicinity of the church tower can hear the organ at night.
sceneCN: 这里 vicinity 是「附近、周边地区」（第 1 个义项：某地周围的一片区域）；句意：学校附近几个村子都能听到铃声。

collocations.phrase: within the vicinity of the campus

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁词干 vicin- 加形容词后缀构成，义为「邻近的；附近地区的」
由拉丁词干 vicin- 加名词后缀构成，义为「邻近地区；附近居民」

senses.title: The area around a place
senses.definition: the surrounding area of a town, building or other place
senses.definitionCN: 城镇、建筑或其他地方四周的区域
senses.example: There are no shops in the vicinity of the new hospital.
senses.why: Latin vicinia means neighbourhood, so the noun names the ring of places and people gathered near one point.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 vicinia 意为「邻里」，所以这个词指的是围绕某一点聚集的一圈地方与人。

senses.title: The state of being near
senses.definition: the condition of being close to a place or thing in space or time
senses.definitionCN: 在空间或时间上靠近某地或某物的状态
senses.example: Visitors are asked to leave the vicinity of the ruins before dark.
senses.exampleCN: 访客被要求在入夜前离开遗迹周边。
senses.why: Neighbourhood also means nearness, so vicinity can stress closeness itself rather than a mapped area.
senses.whyCN: 「邻里」同时也含有「邻近」的意思，因此 vicinity 可以强调靠近这一状态，而不只是画出一片区域。

senses.title: An approximate amount
senses.definition: an amount that is roughly equal to a stated figure
senses.definitionCN: 与所述数字大致相当的量
senses.example: The repairs will cost in the vicinity of a thousand pounds.
senses.exampleCN: 维修费用大约要一千英镑。
senses.why: In the vicinity of also means near to a number, turning spatial nearness into numerical nearness.
senses.whyCN: in the vicinity of 也能表示「接近某个数目」，于是空间上的靠近被转化为数目上的接近。

senses.title: A wide surrounding district
senses.definition: a broad surrounding district, often used in the plural for several such areas
senses.definitionCN: 范围较广的周边地带，常用复数指多片这样的区域
senses.example: Storms moved across the vicinities of three coastal towns.
senses.exampleCN: 风暴横扫了三个沿海城镇的周边地带。
senses.why: The plural vicinities lets the word stretch from a tight ring round one spot to several wider districts.
senses.whyCN: 复数 vicinities 让这个词从一个点的紧密一圈，扩展到多片更宽的周边地带。

intro.en: Vicinity comes from Latin vicinia, a neighbourhood, from vicinus, a neighbour, and vicus, a village or street.
intro.cn: vicinity 来自拉丁语 vicinia（邻里），源于 vicinus（邻居）与 vicus（村庄、街道）。

items.en: Vicus means a village, a street or a row of houses.
items.cn: vicus 意为村庄、街道或一排房屋。

items.en: Vicinus means a neighbour, the person living at the next village or house.
items.cn: vicinus 意为邻居，住在隔壁村子或房子的人。

items.en: Vicinia means a neighbourhood or the state of being near.
items.cn: vicinia 意为邻里，或相邻的状态。

items.en: The noun travels through Old French into Middle English.
items.cn: 这个名词经由古法语进入中古英语。

items.en: Vicinity develops the modern phrase in the vicinity of.
items.cn: vicinity 发展出现代习语 in the vicinity of。

items.en: Modern use extends from places to approximate numbers.
items.cn: 现代用法从具体地点延伸到大致数目。

note.en: Vicinity is the noun of neighbours, close to the Latin stem vicin- and to everyday words for nearby areas.
note.cn: vicinity 是「邻居」之名的名词形式，与拉丁词干 vicin- 以及表示「附近」的常用词相邻。

entries.definition: cruel and violent, a different word entirely
entries.definitionCN: 凶恶的，与 vicinity 只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: the area around where you live
the state of being near in space or time
the things and area around a place

normalIntro.en: Keep the picture of Latin vicinus, the neighbour, and vicinity becomes the circle of neighbours around a spot.
normalIntro.cn: 记住拉丁语 vicinus 那个「邻居」的形象，vicinity 就是围绕某个地点的一圈邻居。

normal.en: Vicinus is a neighbour, and vicinity is the neighbourhood of that neighbour.
normal.cn: vicinus 是邻居，vicinity 就是这位邻居所在的邻里。

normal.en: The fixed phrase is in the vicinity of, never at the vicinity.
normal.cn: 固定说法是 in the vicinity of，不用 at the vicinity。

normal.en: In the vicinity of looks like an address but acts like the word near.
normal.cn: in the vicinity of 看着像个地址，实际起着 near 的作用。

normal.en: Immediate vicinity means the very closest part, within a short walk.
normal.cn: immediate vicinity 指最近的那一小片，几分钟就能走到。

normal.en: Compare neighbourhood: it often suggests a lived-in district, while vicinity is more formal and neutral.
normal.cn: 对比 neighbourhood：它多指有人居住的街区，vicinity 更正式、更中性。

abstract.en: Draw a circle round a house on a map and shade everything within it.
abstract.cn: 在地图上围着一栋房子画个圈，把圈里的地方都涂上颜色。

abstract.en: Hear a bell ring and watch neighbours step out of their doors one by one.
abstract.cn: 听见铃声响起，看着邻居们一扇扇门后陆续走出来。

abstract.en: Hold your palm a little above a table, close but not touching.
abstract.cn: 把手掌悬在桌面上方，很近，却没有碰到。

examples.en: There is a small bakery in the vicinity of the museum.
examples.cn: 博物馆附近有一家小面包店。

examples.en: Police searched the vicinity for any trace of the missing boy.
examples.cn: 警方在附近一带搜寻失踪男孩的线索。

examples.en: The final cost was in the vicinity of five hundred pounds.
examples.cn: 最终花费大约是五百英镑。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「维西」——你住在「维西」村，隔壁就是邻居，附近自然全是邻居；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 vicus（村庄、街道）→ vicinus（邻居）→ vicinia（邻里）→ 古法语 → 英语 vicinity，核心义「邻居们构成的那一圈」。

sensesIntro.en: Vicinity begins as the neighbourhood of neighbours, then stresses nearness, stretches to wide districts, and finally measures approximate amounts.
sensesIntro.cn: vicinity 先指邻居们构成的邻里，再强调靠近这一状态，扩展到宽广地带，最后用于度量大致数目。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a circle drawn around a house, with all its neighbours inside.
core.cn: 核心意象：围绕一栋房子画一个圈，左右邻居都在圈内。

branches.en: The neighbourhood sense names the area around a place.
branches.cn: 邻里义指出一处地方周围的区域。

branches.en: The nearness sense stresses closeness rather than a drawn area.
branches.cn: 邻近义强调靠近本身，而不是划出的区域。

branches.en: One tight round of houses can widen into several broad districts.
branches.cn: 一圈紧凑的房屋可以扩展成几片宽广的地带。

branches.en: Both nearness and wide districts keep the idea of what lies close.
branches.cn: 邻近与宽地带的说法都保留了「就在旁边」的意思。

branches.en: Being near a place becomes being near a number, as in the vicinity of a thousand.
branches.cn: 靠近一个地点变成靠近一个数字，如 the vicinity of a thousand。

intro.en: Vicinity grows from Latin vicinus, a neighbour, and its English relatives are vicinal and vicinage.
intro.cn: vicinity 源自拉丁语 vicinus（邻居），英语中的亲属词有 vicinal 与 vicinage。

latinIntro.en: Latin vicus means village or street, vicinus a neighbour, and vicinia a neighbourhood.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vicus 意为村庄或街道，vicinus 意为邻居，vicinia 意为邻里。

items.example: Vicus names the row of houses where neighbours live.
items.exampleCN: vicus 指邻居们居住的那排房屋。

items.example: Vicinus supplies the stem vicin-.
items.exampleCN: vicinus 提供词干 vicin-。

items.example: Vicinia is the direct source of the English noun.
items.exampleCN: vicinia 是这个英语名词的直接来源。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或性质的名词词尾
items.example: The suffix -ity turns vicin- into vicinity.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ity 把 vicin- 变成 vicinity。

items.example: Vicinity is almost always used with the word in.
items.exampleCN: vicinity 几乎总是和 in 连用。

items.example: The suffix -al forms vicinal.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -al 构成 vicinal。

items.example: Vicinal describes something in the neighbourhood.
items.exampleCN: vicinal 描述位于附近的事物。

items.meaningCN: 表示集合或处所的名词词尾
items.example: The suffix -age forms vicinage.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -age 构成 vicinage。

items.example: Vicinage repeats the neighbourhood sense.
items.exampleCN: vicinage 重复了「邻里」的含义。

definition_en: cruel and violent by nature, very severe, or seriously faulty in a way that keeps getting worse
core_image: 一只龇牙低吼的狗，牙齿间露出明显的缺陷，随时会咬人
scene: 那条狗受过虐待，见人就扑咬。The dog had been badly treated and turned vicious after years of fear.
sceneCN: 这里 vicious 是「凶猛的」（第 1 个义项：凶猛、富有攻击性）；句意：这条狗曾被虐待，多年恐惧之后变得凶猛起来。

derivatives.zh: 由 vicious 加副词后缀构成，义为「凶残地；恶意地」
由 vicious 加名词后缀构成，义为「凶残；恶意」
与 vicious 同源的拉丁词，义为「恶习；罪行」
与 vicious 同源于拉丁 vitium，义为「使失效；败坏」

senses.title: Cruel and violent
senses.definition: cruel and dangerous, likely to attack or harm others by nature or habit
senses.definitionCN: 凶残而危险的，天生或习惯性地容易攻击、伤害他人
senses.example: The farmer kept a vicious dog near the gate.
senses.exampleCN: 农夫在门口养了一条凶猛的狗。
senses.why: Latin vitium first means a fault or blemish, and a creature with a dangerous defect in its nature turns on others.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 vitium 本义是「缺陷、瑕疵」，本性上带着危险缺陷的生物就会扑向他人。

senses.title: Fierce and severe
senses.definition: very strong, fierce and hard to withstand, as of a storm, blow or reaction
senses.definitionCN: 非常强烈、猛烈而难以抵挡的，如风暴、打击或反应
senses.example: The ship was caught in a vicious storm off the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 这艘船在近海遭遇了一场猛烈的风暴。
senses.why: An attack that is fierce is described with the biting force of a vicious animal, so the word widens to storms and blows.
senses.whyCN: 猛烈的攻击让人想到凶兽撕咬的力道，于是这个词也用于风暴与打击。

senses.title: Spiteful and malicious
senses.definition: full of hatred and intended to hurt someone, especially in words
senses.definitionCN: 满怀敌意、意在伤害他人的，尤指言辞
senses.example: She spread vicious rumours about her former partner.
senses.exampleCN: 她散布关于前伴侣的恶毒谣言。
senses.why: The fault in a character becomes an intent to do harm, which is the moral sense of vice hidden in the word.
senses.whyCN: 性格中的「缺陷」变成伤人的意图，这就是藏在词里与 vice 相通的道德义。

senses.title: Worsening itself in a loop
senses.definition: used of a situation that makes its own causes worse each time it repeats
senses.definitionCN: 指一种每次重复都会把自己成因搞得更糟的情境
senses.example: Debt and fear of debt form a vicious cycle.
senses.exampleCN: 债务与对债务的恐惧形成恶性循环。
senses.why: A defect that feeds on itself grows instead of healing, which is exactly what the fixed phrase vicious circle captures.
senses.whyCN: 一个自我滋养的缺陷不会愈合，只会越长越大，这正是固定说法 vicious circle 所捕捉的。

senses.title: Seriously faulty
senses.definition: badly faulty in reasoning or structure, containing a serious logical flaw
senses.definitionCN: 推理或结构上存在严重缺陷的，含有明显的逻辑错误
senses.example: The argument rested on a vicious assumption that everyone agreed.
senses.exampleCN: 这个论证建立在一个错误的假设上，即人人都会同意。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense restored, a plain fault or blemish in something that should be sound.
senses.whyCN: 这恢复了这个词最古老的含义：本该完好之物上的一个纯粹缺陷。

intro.en: Vicious comes from Latin vitiosus, faulty, from vitium, a fault or vice, through Old French vicious.
intro.cn: vicious 来自拉丁语 vitiosus（有缺陷的），源于 vitium（缺陷、恶习），经由古法语 vicious 进入英语。

items.en: Vitium means a fault, defect or moral vice.
items.cn: vitium 意为缺陷、瑕疵或道德上的恶习。

items.en: The adjective vitiosus means faulty, defective or corrupt.
items.cn: 形容词 vitiosus 意为有缺陷的、败坏的。

items.en: Old French vicious carries the faulty sense northwards.
items.cn: 古法语 vicious 把「有缺陷」的含义带向北方。

items.en: Middle English vicious first means full of faults or morally bad.
items.cn: 中古英语 vicious 最初指充满缺陷或道德败坏的。

items.en: The word sharpens towards cruel animals and malicious people.
items.cn: 这个词逐渐偏向指凶猛的动物与心怀恶意的人。

items.en: Modern English adds the vicious circle of self-worsening problems.
items.cn: 现代英语又添上 vicious circle 这种自我恶化的循环。

note.en: Vicious is the Latin fault word turned savage, close to vice and vitiate, and to English words for cruel and fierce.
note.cn: vicious 是拉丁语「缺陷」之词变得凶恶的结果，与 vice、vitiate 以及表示「凶残、猛烈」的英语词相邻。

entries.definition: the area around a place, a different word entirely
entries.definitionCN: 附近，与 vicious 只是拼写相近，词源不同

normalIntro.en: Hold the Latin fault word vitium at the centre, and vicious is a fault that has grown teeth.
normalIntro.cn: 把拉丁语「缺陷」之词 vitium 放在中心，vicious 就是长出獠牙的缺陷。

normal.en: Vitium is a fault, and vicious is that fault grown dangerous.
normal.cn: vitium 是缺陷，vicious 是这缺陷变得危险。

normal.en: The noun vice and the verb vitiate come from the same Latin fault word.
normal.cn: 名词 vice 与动词 vitiate 都出自同一个拉丁语「缺陷」之词。

normal.en: A vicious circle is a ring of faults that keeps feeding itself.
normal.cn: vicious circle 就是一圈不断自我喂养的毛病。

normal.en: Vicious attack, vicious dog and vicious criticism all keep the biting energy.
normal.cn: vicious attack、vicious dog、vicious criticism 都保留了「撕咬」般的力道。

normal.en: Compare savage: it stresses wildness, while vicious stresses the cruel intent and the hidden fault.
normal.cn: 对比 savage：它强调野性，vicious 则强调残忍的意图与背后的缺陷。

abstract.en: See a guard dog pulling a short chain, teeth bared at the gate.
abstract.cn: 想象一条看门狗绷紧短链，在门口龇牙咧嘴。

abstract.en: Watch a storm hammer the cliff and throw the waves back up.
abstract.cn: 想象风暴猛击悬崖，把浪头一次次抛回空中。

abstract.en: Picture a rumour passed from mouth to mouth, growing sharper at each step.
abstract.cn: 想象一则谣言从一张嘴传到另一张嘴，每传一步都更尖刻。

examples.en: The guard dogs in that yard are reported to be vicious.
examples.cn: 据说那个院子里的看门狗很凶。

examples.en: Lack of sleep and stress can set up a vicious cycle.
examples.cn: 缺觉与压力可以形成恶性循环。

examples.en: She was stung by a vicious remark from a colleague.
examples.cn: 她被同事一句恶毒的话刺痛了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「威赦」——凶兽扑来时，人们大声求「威赦」，场面凶险；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 vitium（缺陷、恶习）→ vitiosus（有缺陷的）→ 古法语 vicious → 英语 vicious，核心义「有缺陷」→「本性败坏」→「凶恶」。

sensesIntro.en: Vicious starts from the plain idea of a fault, then takes on cruelty in creatures, malice in words, severity in weather and logic, and finally the self-worsening loop.
sensesIntro.cn: vicious 从「有缺陷」这个朴素观念出发，在生物身上变成凶残，在言语中变成恶意，在天气与推理中变成猛烈与谬误，最后落到自我恶化的循环。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a snarling dog whose bared teeth show a visible fault.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只低吼的狗，龇出的牙间显露着明显的缺陷。

branches.en: A dangerous fault in a creature becomes cruelty and attack.
branches.cn: 生物身上危险的缺陷变成凶残与攻击。

branches.en: The biting force widens to fierce storms and heavy blows.
branches.cn: 撕咬般的力道扩展到猛烈的风暴与重击。

branches.en: A moral fault turns into words meant to wound.
branches.cn: 道德上的缺陷变成意在伤人的言辞。

branches.en: A flaw in logic and a flaw that feeds itself are both plain defects.
branches.cn: 逻辑上的谬误与自我喂养的缺陷，都是纯粹的缺陷。

branches.en: A vicious animal and a vicious circle both keep hurting what touches them.
branches.cn: 凶兽与恶性循环都会不断伤到碰到它们的事物。

intro.en: Vicious is built on the Latin stem viti-, with English vice, vitiate, viciously and viciousness around it.
intro.cn: vicious 建立在拉丁词干 viti- 之上，周围有英语的 vice、vitiate、viciously 与 viciousness。

latinIntro.en: Latin vitium means a fault, and vitiosus means faulty or corrupt.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vitium 意为缺陷，vitiosus 意为有缺陷的或败坏的。

items.example: Vitium supplies the fault at the core of the word.
items.exampleCN: vitium 提供这个词核心处的「缺陷」。

items.example: Vitiosus is the direct ancestor of the English adjective.
items.exampleCN: vitiosus 是这个英语形容词的直接祖先。

items.example: The suffix -ous makes vicious describe something full of faults.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ous 让 vicious 表示「满是缺陷」。

items.meaningCN: 恶毒的；猛烈的；有缺陷的
items.example: Vicious keeps the fault but adds teeth.
items.exampleCN: vicious 保留了「缺陷」，又添上了獠牙。

items.example: Vice is the noun of the same Latin fault.
items.exampleCN: vice 是同一个拉丁「缺陷」之词的名词形式。

items.example: Vitiate keeps the bare idea of spoiling.
items.exampleCN: vitiate 保留了「败坏」的赤裸含义。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms viciously.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 viciously。

items.example: Viciously describes the manner of an attack.
items.exampleCN: viciously 描述攻击的方式。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms viciousness.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ness 构成 viciousness。

items.example: Viciousness names the quality itself.
items.exampleCN: viciousness 表示这种性质本身。
